findings: Windows acceptance covers host-profile catalog checks for Python file/class/module-function, built-in, C ABI, and external process hosts.
Negative cases reject unsupported capability requirements before strategy factory or handler dispatch; external-process tests also reject a mismatched host identity acknowledgment.
The legacy C ABI test confirms plugins without the optional requirement export remain compatible when requirements are empty, while unsupported FillUpdates fails before plugin creation.
Runtime Python class and module-function tests exercise production Runtime catalogs across the four supported transports; local backtest construction rejects Runtime-only requirements.
The built-in worker path accepts Bar for SMA and rejects unsupported Timer and MultiInstrument requirements before dispatch.
limitations: This review accepts the Windows host matrix only. Targeted Linux Rust dispatch, legacy C ABI, and Python negotiation checks are configured in CI but have not yet produced Linux evidence.
The historical failed runs are not counted as passing evidence; the reviewed run IDs are the later successful corrections.
